To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1H MR spectroscopy studies suggest that glutamatergically‐based abnormalities may be present in the anterior cingulate cortex of adolescents with ADHD, and that these abnormalities appear to normalize with MPH treatment.

1) Glutamate, Glutamine, and Glutamate +Glutamine ratios are higher in untreated adolescents with ADHD, compared to healthy comparators; 2) these group differences are not present in adolescents with ADHD treated with OROS MPH; 3) these findings are suggestive of the presence of glutamate abnormalities in ADHD youth which may be reversed with OROS MPH treatment; 4) the results are preliminary, and need to be replicated in a larger, controlled study
